terms.gloss: you’re making fun of me, you’re kidding
terms.grammar: lūdō with the person as object: “you are playing with me”
evidence: Hor. S. 2.5.58: an prūdēns lūdis mē obscūra canendō? (Lewis & Short), s.v. furō

terms.grammar: nē with the present subjunctive, a prohibition
evidence: Plaut. Curc. 326: vidē nē mē lūdās, mind you’re not kidding me
terms.comment: In comedy; in prose a prohibition prefers nē with the perfect subjunctive or nōlī with the infinitive.

evidence: Plaut. Most. 1081: sciō, jocāris nunc tū, I know, you’re joking now

sources: Lewis & Short: ludo · Lewis & Short: jocor
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 101, 336, checked against the searchable text and the page image.
